subject: Production 429 spike after quota cutover - Mediconnect
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@mediconnect.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Chen <tchen@mediconnect.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: production 429 spike since quota cutover

Hey Ben,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and timeouts on our production API calls starting ~08:50 PT after the quota tiering cutover. Traffic pattern looks normal on our side — same request volume — but the error rate jumped to ~18% and several upstream services cascaded retries which caused downstream timeouts. Attached are a few response samples and a short error trace from this morning.

Impact: several patient-facing features degraded (search and appointment booking). This is high severity for us. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side in the last deploy/window? We need an immediate mitigation plan and ETA for resolution.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lewis
Head of Platform, Mediconnect
Sara.Lewis@mediconnect.com

Attachments: client-429-samples.json (json), error_trace_20270220.log (text)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@mediconnect.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production 429 spike since quota cutover

Sara — sorry for the trouble and thanks for the quick samples. We did a scheduled quota tiering cutover at 08:45 PT for a subset of orgs (per the rollout plan). Initial hypothesis: a mapping error caused a small number of Mediconnect projects to be assigned to the default low-tier, triggering tight per-project limits. That would explain a sudden 429 spike with normal traffic.

Immediate next steps I’m asking for now:
- Rishi: can you validate project->tier mapping and confirm whether Mediconnect projects were affected?
- Marissa: please prepare a rollback of the cutover for impacted projects if Rishi confirms.
- Naomi: I’ll need an exec ping/path for credits and a short customer note.

Sara — we’ll triage and come back with a mitigation timeline within 20 minutes. Would you like us to enable a temporary soft-limit increase while we validate?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: production 429 spike since quota cutover

Quick update from infra: confirmed — 5 Mediconnect projects were incorrectly assigned to the default "bronze" project tier due to a label-parsing edge case in the tiering script. The ruleset maps by org label and project alias; a new alias pattern introduced by the migration slipped through validation. Affected projects are currently hitting per-project token caps which produce 429s; client retries amplified the effect.

Mitigation plan (I can run these in parallel):
1) Immediate: temporarily bump the per-project soft limits for the 5 projects to match their previous tier (10 minutes) to stop the 429s and allow traffic to stabilize.
2) Short-term (20–40m): rollback the tiering change for Mediconnect (re-assign those projects to their previous tier) and re-deploy corrected mapping.
3) Post-mortem: patch the tiering script with stricter alias validation and add a canary that checks mapping for top-20 orgs before rollout.

I will execute step 1 now unless you tell me not to — this will require a short config change with negligible risk and immediate benefit. Runbook: https://redwood-internal.runbooks/rollback-2027-02-20 (internal).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Urgent: production 429 spike since quota cutover — immediate mitigation

Sara / Tom — thanks for patience. Our infra team just applied a temporary soft-limit bump to the affected projects and is starting the rollback of the tiering mapping now. Expected stabilization in ~8–12 minutes.

Planned customer-facing steps:
- Immediate (now): soft-limit bump to stop 429s.
- 30m: rollback mapping and validated deploy of corrected tiering script.
- 1–2h: internal post-mortem and follow-up with a written summary + credits.

Would you like us to pause retries client-side for a short window while we reconcile? That will speed recovery on your side. Also confirming we will provide a one-time credit for the incident — Naomi is on copy for approval.

Ben

Sara
